source_notes.finding: Each TanStack tool becomes a guest function external_<name>; the model gets TypeScript stubs generated from the tools' JSON Schema in the system prompt (createCodeModeSystemPrompt) and the function names in the tool description.

Eager tools get full stubs up front. Tools marked lazy: true appear by name only, and a separate discover_tools tool returns their stubs on demand, so large catalogs need not put every schema in the prompt.

Each tool is an ivm.Reference to an async host function stored on the guest global as __<name>_ref; the guest wrapper calls applySyncPromise with JSON, which blocks the isolate until the host settles. That makes calls serial.

isolated-vm V8 isolate in the host process. Docs claim no access to host file system, network or process; P3 to P5 and P12 agree. The raw References being reachable from guest code is wider than needed, though no escape through them was found.
execute returns { success, result, logs, error }; result is JSON.stringify'd inside the isolate and parsed on the host. No truncation anywhere in this driver.
Only timeout and memoryLimit, both set per createCodeModeTool. No output, call-count or concurrency limit.
A new isolate per execution, disposed in finally. The cleanup disposes again after isolated-vm already disposed on OOM, which throws out of execute (P7).
Errors are normalized to { name, message, stack }; tool errors are passed to the guest as plain messages and reach the model verbatim. Line numbers are not mapped back past the wrapper.

Rejects tools with needsApproval at construction; warns (or throws, by option) when a tool input schema has parameter names like password, token or apiKey, to stop the model passing secrets through code; input and output schemas are validated on the host per call. MIT, last commit 2026-11-21.

surprises: The docs say the three Promise.all weather calls "run in parallel inside the sandbox" (code-mode.md:116), but with the Node driver they run one after another (P9, 1,030 ms for 5 calls).

At the memory limit, execute() throws "Isolate is already disposed" from its own cleanup instead of returning the memory error it had already built, so callers that rely on execute never throwing get an exception.

Raw isolated-vm Reference objects (__external_lookup_ref, __captureLog) are guest globals; guest code can call the tool host function directly, skipping the wrapper. No escape was found through them in P12g to P12j.
Host tool error messages reach the model verbatim (P10c printed the fake DSN), unlike the Vercel layers, which replace them with a generic message.
Driver creation spawns a Node subprocess once to check isolated-vm compatibility (213 ms setup).
